A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered sections and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, user studies, ablations, expert audits, and verifier comparisons in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds an uncertainty baseline comparison and further expert-agreement results.

M1.justification: The Visual Fidelity verification pipeline, Contrastiveness masking and entailment procedure, and score-combination rules remain unchanged. The added P(True) procedure is evaluated as a baseline.

E1.justification: Both versions use A-OKVQA, VizWiz, and MMMU-Pro, including the generated-distractor scenario and user studies on A-OKVQA and VizWiz. The additions retain existing task and dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix H adds P(True) to the LLaVA-v1.5-7B comparison on A-OKVQA and MMMU-Pro, alongside retained logit confidence and explanation-quality scores (v2 Table 12; v3 Table 13). Other comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The 100-example human-alignment audit changes from one expert to two independent experts (v2 Appendix J.1; v3 Appendix K.1). The added P(True) evaluation introduces a correctness-query and logit-scoring procedure. Existing benchmark splits and user-study protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The score-validation audit is expanded to examine agreement between experts and consistency of automated-score agreement across experts. Existing hard-negative ablations, verifier robustness tests, presentation ablations, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix K.1 introduces inter-annotator reliability reporting using Cohen's kappa, alongside separate human–automated-score agreements. v2 reported only one expert's agreement with automated scores. Existing t-tests, bootstrap tests, and error-bar reporting remain unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 Table 13 adds P(True) discriminability/ECE results of 0.032/0.253 on A-OKVQA and -0.001/0.772 on MMMU-Pro. Appendix K.1 adds inter-expert kappas of 0.68/0.46 for VF/Contrastiveness and second-expert–automated-score kappas of 0.49/0.39; the original 0.51/0.44 are retained. Main benchmark and user-study results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions, mathematical reasoning, and discriminability definition remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised; the new kappa values are empirical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and central findings, including the two complementary explanation qualities and the reported 11.1 percentage-point user-accuracy improvement and 15.4-point reduction in false acceptance.

C2.justification: Appendix H extends the interpretation of poor uncertainty calibration on complex reasoning tasks to P(True). Appendix K.1 newly interprets expert agreement as supporting a well-defined annotation task and consistent validation. Existing limitations and other interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds the exact P(True) prompt and explains selecting maximum affirmative/negative token logits before softmax normalization in Table 12. It also discloses the audit annotators' expertise and author/independent status. Existing code access and implementation details remain available.

R1.justification: The reference list and Appendix A related-work discussion are unchanged. The additional comparison evidence does not revise the paper's novelty claims or its explanation-quality and decision-support positioning.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify study counts and random-score presentation, expand the baseline and audit descriptions, and add a heading around existing qualitative examples. v3 removes the contradictory statement that VizWiz Contrastiveness was not computed and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figures 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8 are redrawn with typography and spacing changes while retaining their data; Figure 2 consolidates its color bars. v3 adds a baseline-prompt table and comparison row, clarifies Figure 9d's caption, and makes accompanying layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The independent second expert and inter-annotator agreement strengthen the previously single-expert alignment check. P(True) and its documented implementation modestly broaden the comparison, while removing the contradictory VizWiz statement improves consistency. These are limited gains: agreement remains moderate and the principal methods and results are unchanged.
